newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Mittal plans $2.8 billion listing.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Mittal plans $2.8 billion listing.

text.p: Lakshmi Mittal, one of Britain's wealthiest businessmen who has made a fortune turning around money-losing steel companies worldwide, is planning a $2.8 billion stock market flotation, sources said Wednesday.

Sources close to the issue said Mittal, 47, plans to raise about $450 million by selling a 16 percent stake in his family-owned Ispat International company, which will be listed on the New York and Amsterdam stock exchanges.
Formed in 1989 and based in the Netherlands, Ispat International now owns steel mills in Canada, Ireland, Germany, Mexico and the Caribbean.

The sources told Reuters that about 19.25 million shares are expected to be listed in the $22-$26 range. The issue is being handled by Credit Suisse First Boston and Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette. The prospectus for the issue is due to be published next week.
The company reported net profits of about $615 million on revenues of $1.8 billion in 1996 and on an annual output of nearly 6 million metric tons of steel.
After paying off a loan of $90 million, Ispat will use the bulk of the funds generated by the sale on capital expenditures.
Mittal's larger holding company, LNM Group, recorded revenues of more than $2.7 billion, including operations in Indonesia and Kazakhstan which will not be part of the flotation.

Specialising in both flat and long products made in electric mini-arc mills instead of the usual blast furnaces, Ispat's first major breakthrough was the acquisition of what is now Caribbean Ispat in Trinidad and Tobago.

Since then, Ispat has taken over Sidbec-Dosco in Canada, the formerly government-owned Irish Steel and Hamberger Stahlwerker in Germany. The company is also buying two mills from Thyssen Stahl in Germany.
